located_point.method: Bare mound surface at the northern edge of the modern villages in the Sentinel-2 median composite (UTM 43N E 608112 N 3240897), 190 m south-west of the Wikidata starting point; the mounds RGR-1 to RGR-7 shown on the mound dispersal map (Nath report Fig. 1, PDF p. 336) lie partly under the villages and fields around this point and could not be delimited individually at 10 m.

sources.result: No line measured. The modern villages of Rakhi Khas and Rakhi Shahpur cover the central mounds; bare mound patches north of them show no straight feature, and without a plan of excavated architecture nothing in the image can be identified as Harappan.

sources.citation: Amarendra Nath, Excavations at Rakhigarhi, 1997-2000 (Archaeological Survey of India), Internet Archive scan excavationsatrakhigarhi19972000amarendranath_457_Z.
sources.result: Inspected PDF pp. 88-125 (cuttings, stratigraphy and structural remains), 336 (Fig. 1, mound dispersal with contours, north arrow, no architecture). The figures in the structural chapters are hand-drawn sections (pp. 99-101) and photographs (pp. 102, 123-125); there is no plan of excavated architecture.

notes: Not measurable. Held sources checked: the Nath report; Indian Archaeology - A Review 1997-98 (pp. 61-66, photographs), 1998-99 (pp. 20-23, text and photographs), 1999-2000 (pp. 37-41, text) and 2011-12 (pp. 30-36, DEM, survey and ceramic distribution maps). A web search for an open plan of the 2013-16 or later excavations found only news pages.
plan_search: No plan of Harappan architecture with a north arrow was found in held or openly available sources (21 October 2026).
stated_orientation_encounters: Nath report p. 119 (structural remains text) describes a lane as 'running North-South'; sections on pp. 99 and 101 are labelled 'section facing east' and 'section facing north'; a web-search summary of news coverage (livehistoryindia.com and organiser.org results, 21 October 2026) described an RGR-1 street as running east-west. None was used.
unmeasurable_reason: No plan found: no held or openly available plan of excavated Harappan architecture at Rakhigarhi has a north arrow (the ASI report gives sections, photographs and a mound map). Features not resolvable at 10 m: the central mounds lie under the modern villages, and no straight Harappan feature can be identified in the imagery.
